workstream: U35 -- explicit reference-offset hook in gait.py (replaces the paused joint-offset residual direction)

background.why_this_exists: Sampled zero-mean ankle-roll RESIDUAL exploration (CaraResidualEnv, U34) was found to reliably preserve the nominal gait everywhere EXCEPT a narrow, magnitude-insensitive window at the phase-A->B weight-transfer onset, where even 0.0005 rad noise caused falls ~50-65% of the time. Per the user's own stated stop-condition ('if nominal sampled behavior is too fragile even at very small residuals, stop direct ankle-offset exploration'), that finding was treated as meeting the stop-condition, and direct ankle-offset residual learning was paused in favor of 'corrections to the teacher's balance reference or parameters.'
background.mechanism_identified: gait.py's U9 lateral roll-trim (take_step -> ss_step) latches a balance reference st['ref_ey'] = ey (CoM-to-stance-foot lateral offset, world Y axis, metres) from a SINGLE INSTANTANEOUS SAMPLE at the first controller update of phase B, then regulates dy = ey - ref_ey for the rest of the step. This single-sample latch, occurring exactly at the fragile transition previously found, is a credible mechanism for the fragility -- but source inspection alone does not establish it is the (sole) cause; that requires an intervention, per the tests below.
background.constraint: gait.py was previously treated as a hard, unmodified gate for the whole project (frozen generator/validator). That was an experimental-isolation choice, not a permanent requirement, per explicit instruction this turn -- so a minimal, explicit, EXPLICITLY OPTIONAL hook was added to gait.py itself (reference_offset_fn, default None => identical behaviour), rather than trying to reach ref_ey non-invasively (impossible: it is a plain local Python float, never crossing any boundary the existing mj_step-monkeypatch technique can intercept).

gait_py_change.diff_summary: run(config, n_steps, view, json_path, baseline_path, reference_offset_fn=None) -- new KEYWORD-ONLY-by-convention parameter, default None, so every existing positional call site (main(), _TeacherThread._run in cara_residual_env.py) is untouched and unaffected. Inside ss_step: `ref_ey_effective = st['ref_ey'] + _ref_offset_fn(st['ref_ey'])` replaces the old `dy = ey - st['ref_ey']` with `dy = ey - ref_ey_effective`. The stored latch st['ref_ey'] itself is NEVER overwritten by the offset -- kept separate per instruction, so 'offset back to zero' has an unambiguous meaning. KPA, KDA, KPH left untouched, as instructed.
gait_py_change.units_and_sign: ey = com_y - stance_foot_y (world-frame Y/lateral axis, metres), from ss_step's own definition. reference_offset_fn(ref_ey) receives the step's already-latched reference (metres, same convention) and returns an offset (metres, same convention) added to it. A positive offset raises the effective reference, which (since dy = ey - ref_ey_effective) REDUCES the trim's correction for a given +Y CoM excursion and INCREASES it for a -Y one, relative to the unmodified teacher.
gait_py_change.frozen_baseline: cara_description/scripts/gait_frozen_baseline.py -- byte-for-byte copy of gait.py immediately before this change, kept as an independent ground truth; not imported by any production path.
gait_py_change.regression_check: python3 gait.py --steps 2 after the edit: MILESTONE MET, 57mm total advance, 0.9deg final tilt, PASS/PASS -- identical to the pre-edit reference run.

test1_zero_offset_equivalence.method: Ran gait.py (default reference_offset_fn=None) and gait_frozen_baseline.py side by side, both with mujoco.mj_step monkeypatched (non-invasive, standard technique) to record qpos and ctrl at every physics substep; compared the FULL trajectory, not just endpoint metrics.
test1_zero_offset_equivalence.result: PASS -- bit-for-bit identical. 23,650 substeps compared, 19-dim qpos, max_abs_diff(qpos)=0.0, max_abs_diff(ctrl)=0.0.
test1_zero_offset_equivalence.conclusion: The hook's zero-default genuinely reproduces the pre-hook teacher exactly; the refactor introduced no behavioural change by default.

test2_causal_latch.method: A one-time lateral CoM-velocity kick (data.qvel[1] += kick) applied 40ms before step_idx=0's phase-B onset (identical pre-latch state across trials, by construction of a deterministic simulation). Calibration swept kick in [0.001, 0.002, 0.004, 0.008, 0.015] m/s with reference_offset_fn recording (not altering) the resulting latch, to find a kick that both measurably biases the latch (chosen threshold: >0.5mm) AND produces a materially worse outcome, before running the actual (b)-vs-(c) causal comparison.
test2_causal_latch.calibration_result: kick <= 0.004 m/s: latch biased by only 0.02-0.10mm, fully recovered (tilt ~4.3deg, exit_code=0, matches the ~4.4deg unperturbed baseline). kick >= 0.008 m/s: catastrophic, uncontrolled 180deg tip-over (exit_code=1) -- but the resulting latch bias at THAT kick was only 0.19-0.36mm, i.e. SMALLER than the >0.5mm threshold intended to guarantee the bias itself was large enough to matter. No tested kick magnitude produced both a large (>0.5mm) latch bias AND a merely-degraded (not already-catastrophic) outcome.
test2_causal_latch.result: INCONCLUSIVE with this disturbance family -- reported as such, not forced to a conclusion. The intended (b) [perturbed, own latch] vs (c) [perturbed, nominal latch substituted] comparison could not be run meaningfully, because there is no intermediate kick magnitude in this sweep where the disturbance is survivable-but-degraded rather than either fully absorbed or already catastrophic.
test2_causal_latch.interpretation_disclosed_not_overclaimed: This itself is informative: it suggests a sharp dynamic bifurcation in the underlying mechanics at this phase transition (values below ~0.005 m/s fully absorbed, values above ~0.007 m/s catastrophic, with almost no graded middle ground) rather than a graceful degradation that a 'wrong reference value' story alone would predict. This casts some doubt on whether a reference-level correction can help against a disturbance of THIS TYPE (a lateral momentum/velocity kick) at THIS phase -- the CoM trajectory may already be dynamically unrecoverable by the time any reference-based correction could act. It does NOT rule out that reference corrections could still help against smaller, more gradual disturbances, or against a different disturbance channel (e.g. a torque/moment kick, or a finer sweep between 0.004 and 0.008 m/s) -- neither has been tried.
test2_causal_latch.not_done: A finer-grained kick sweep between 0.004 and 0.008 m/s, and/or a different disturbance channel (moment kick, longer/gentler push), which could still locate a usable intermediate regime -- flagged as a possible next micro-step, not run yet (scope discipline: this was meant to be a short probe).

test3_small_smooth_offset_probe.method: On the fully UNPERTURBED nominal run (no kick), a constant reference_offset was smoothly ramped on (0.4s smoothstep) at the start of step_idx=0's phase B, held through phases B+C+D, and ramped back to exactly zero before phase E (transfer) -- magnitudes chosen (0.2/0.5/1.0mm) so that KPA*offset stays within the ~0.05 rad envelope probe_phase_pulse.py (U34/U35 prep) already established as bidirectionally safe for direct ankle-roll JOINT residual pulses -- an earlier attempt at 2/5/10mm (implying 0.1-0.5 rad corrections) was a scale-calibration miss, not a hook finding, and is superseded by these numbers.
test3_small_smooth_offset_probe.internal_consistency_check: For every SAFE trial, the recorded delta_ctrl on r_ankle_roll matched the trim law's own algebra (delta_ctrl = -sfn*KPA*offset) to within numerical noise (max_err 0.03-0.06, vs. control magnitudes ~0.1-1.0). This confirms the hook is wired correctly and doing exactly what the formula says -- it is not a bug in the mechanism. For every FAILING trial the check breaks down badly (max_err ~10-22), consistent with the robot having already inverted (state saturated, the small-perturbation algebra no longer applies), not with a hook malfunction.

result.negative_offsets (-0.2, -0.5, -1.0 mm): ALL SAFE. tilt ~4.4deg (matches baseline's 4.39deg closely), exit_code=0, touchdown continues normally after step 0.
result.positive_offsets (+0.2, +0.5, +1.0 mm): ALL FAIL. Every magnitude, including the smallest tested (+0.2mm, implying just a 0.01 rad ctrl correction), produces a catastrophic, uncontrolled 180deg tip-over on the completely UNDISTURBED nominal walk.

test3_small_smooth_offset_probe.explicit_flag_not_yet_isolated: This sign-dependent asymmetry closely parallels the EARLIER ankle-roll joint-offset asymmetry (U34's probe_residual_bound.py: constant -0.001 rad failed, +0.005 rad survived) that turned out to be a whole-episode/sustained-bias CONFOUND, not a fundamental sign-sensitivity -- resolved only once brief, phase-indexed, per-leg pulses (probe_phase_pulse.py) showed clean bidirectional symmetry. The SAME confounds are present here and have NOT yet been ruled out: (1) only ONE stance leg/step (r_ankle_roll, step_idx=0, lead=l_) was tested -- the other leg/step (l_ankle_roll, step_idx=1) has not; (2) the offset was SUSTAINED across nearly the whole step (B+C+D, ~6000 controller updates), not a BRIEF pulse like the joint-space probes that established symmetry; (3) the natural drift direction of ey during this specific step/stance was not independently characterized, so it is not yet known whether '+offset' happens to ask the trim to tolerate MORE of whatever direction the CoM is already drifting toward (plausibly destabilizing by construction) versus a leg/topology-specific sign effect. Per the lesson already learned twice in this project (U27, U34->U35), this asymmetry is reported as REAL AND MEASURED, but NOT YET CONCLUDED to be a fundamental property of positive reference offsets in general.
test3_small_smooth_offset_probe.recommended_next_micro_step_not_yet_run: Repeat this exact probe as a BRIEF, phase-indexed pulse (ramp on/off within ~0.5-1s, not sustained across the whole step) on BOTH stance legs (r_ankle_roll/step_idx=0 AND l_ankle_roll/step_idx=1), matching the design that successfully disambiguated the earlier joint-offset case.

decision_point_for_user: No PPO run yet, per instruction. Two open items before any learning: (1) test 2's causal latch test came back genuinely inconclusive with the tested kick family -- needs either a finer kick sweep or a different disturbance channel to become conclusive, or an explicit decision to proceed without it; (2) test 3's positive/negative asymmetry needs the same phase-indexed, both-legs, brief-pulse treatment that resolved the analogous joint-offset confound before it can be trusted as a real (not confounded) effect.
not_done_this_turn: No PPO, no training, no gains exposed, no restructuring of the gait controller (all per explicit instruction). The reference_offset_fn hook itself was NOT used to build any environment/policy interface yet -- that is future work contingent on resolving the two open items above.
